out:
{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that being the 'weak link' on a team with an Internet partner would lead to longer exercise duration compared to exercising alone, and that verbal encouragement from the partner would further increase exercise duration.",
  "design": "mixed, 3 (condition: individual control, partner with-encouragement, partner-without-encouragement) x 2 (performance block: Block 1 & Block 2) factorial design.",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Participants were assigned to exercise alone or with a virtual partner (confederate). In partner conditions, participants were told they were part of a 2-person team where the team score was determined by the first person to quit (conjunctive task). Participants were led to believe they were the 'weak link' via manipulated feedback. In the encouragement condition, participants received prerecorded verbal encouragement from the partner.",
  "outcome_measure": "Total duration of exercise (in seconds) held across five abdominal plank exercises.",
  "population_and_setting": "College students recruited from introductory psychology and kinesiology courses at a large Midwestern university, tested in a laboratory setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 115,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via online and face-to-face systems; participants received course credit.",
  "analysis_plan": "3 (Condition: Individuals, Partner-without-encouragement, Partner-with-encouragement) x 2 (Sex) ANOVA on exercise duration difference scores (Block 2 - Block 1).",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used a PlayStation 2 exercise video game (EyeToy: Kinetic) to perform isometric abdominal planks. Participants in partner conditions interacted via a prerecorded video link. Data were collected in two waves; the first wave did not include the encouragement condition."
}
